issues.display_title: Issue #519: Add Status Follower in API Search User
issues.main_description_html:
Implementation: Search User — Followed Status

Issue: #519 (follow-up to #451)

Route

GET /search/user?search=&page=&limit=
Authorization: <JWT token>

Unchanged route and query params; only the response gains a field.

Changes

  • Models/SearchModel.go: added a Followed bool field to SearchUser, tagged json:"followed" and gorm:"-". It is gorm:"-" because the value comes from a separate followers lookup, not from the followers_counts select.
  • Action/V1/Search/SearchUser.go: captured the caller's user id into a new myUserId variable inside the existing role == "user" block (from the UserFunctions.UserDatas call already made there), and set Followed for each result inside the loop that already fetches each user's 4 recent posts.
  • Did not change the query, pagination, ordering, filters, or any existing response field.

Data Flow

  1. Role and encrypt come from the auth middleware locals; the handler already rejects anything other than "user" or "viewer" with 401.
  2. For role == "user", UserFunctions.UserDatas(c, encrypt) is already called to validate the account and read last_login; the same map now also supplies user_id, stored in myUserId. Viewers never enter that block, so myUserId stays empty for them.
  3. The search query against followers_counts runs unchanged.
  4. In the per-result loop, after the recent-posts query, Followed is resolved with UserFunctions.CheckFollowed(myUserId, rowSearchUser[i].ID) — the same helper Action/V1/Users/ProfileFollower.go and ProfileFollowing.go use, so the meaning of "followed" stays identical across endpoints.
  5. The lookup is skipped entirely when myUserId is empty, so viewers get followed: false without any extra query.

Behaviour

  • Authenticated user: true when a followers row exists with user_id = the result's id and follower_id = the caller.
  • Viewer (unauthenticated): always false.
  • The caller's own account, when it appears in its own search results: false, since no self-follow row exists.

Files

  • src/Models/SearchModel.go
  • src/Action/V1/Search/SearchUser.go
  • src/Action/V1/Search/SearchUser_test.go (new)

Verification

gofmt -l src/Action/V1/Search/SearchUser.go src/Models/SearchModel.go
go build ./...
go vet ./src/Action/V1/Search/ ./src/Models/
go test ./src/Action/V1/Search/

Results: build, vet, and gofmt clean on the touched files; package tests pass, including the new
TestSearchUserResponseExposesFollowedAndHidesIdentifiers, which asserts the marshalled payload
contains "followed" and still omits id and encrypt.

Note: gofmt -l src/Action/V1/Search/ reports seven other files in the package as unformatted. They
were already unformatted before this change and were left untouched.

Not yet done: manual smoke test against a running server with a real follow relationship.

Known gaps

  • One followers query per result row (at most limit, default 8) on top of the recent-posts query
    the loop already ran. This matches the existing N+1 shape of this handler and of
    ProfileFollower.go. If the search limit is ever raised well above 8, replace it with a single
    WHERE user_id IN (?) AND follower_id = ? lookup and a map.

Git

Branch development.

Changes

Implementation: Handle Missing Elasticsearch Counters in Collection Detail

Changes

  • Added a safe fallback when Elasticsearch returns no counter document for a collection post.
  • Returned zero values for counter_view, counter_like, and counter_comment instead of indexing an empty result.
  • Preserved existing counter data when the Elasticsearch document exists.
  • Added regression tests for both missing and existing Elasticsearch counter data.

Files

  • src/Action/V1/CollectionPost/CollectionPostDetail.go
  • src/Action/V1/CollectionPost/CollectionPostDetail_test.go

Result: all packages pass.

Problem

GET /posts/collection-detail/:sid panicked with runtime error: index out of range [0] with length 0 when a post existed in the collection view but its Elasticsearch counter document was missing. The handler accessed postCounts[0] without checking whether the result was empty.

Affected example:

/posts/collection-detail/XmzE7c5866606d-20260828083540-f37937bcf155

Scope

  • Use the existing zero-counter behavior already used by other post-list endpoints.
  • Preserve the endpoint response contract and unrelated behavior.
  • Add focused regression coverage.

Acceptance Criteria

  • The collection-detail endpoint does not panic when Elasticsearch returns an empty counter result.
  • Missing counter documents produce zero view, like, and comment counters.
  • Existing Elasticsearch counter documents are returned unchanged.
  • Full Go test suite passes.

  • Update matching Redis package internals.
  • Preserve routes, queries, response shapes, filtering rules, ordering, pagination, and encryption behavior.
  • Keep all *Slim.go files unchanged.

issues.main_description_html:
Implementation: Centralize Followings Redis String-List Reads

Summary

Reused the existing Redis.GetEncodedStringList(ctx, key) helper for both non-slim _list_followings_ readers. The refactor changes 2 Go files with 3 added lines and 15 removed lines. Slim files remain untouched.

Changes

  • Replaced the manual followings Redis/base64/JSON decoder in Redis.SuggestionUser with the package-local helper call.
  • Replaced the equivalent decoder in Posts.TimeLinePostJustForYou with Redis.GetEncodedStringList.
  • Changed the timeline followings slice from []interface{} to []string to match the Redis payload contract and the existing Redis.SuggestionUser consumer.
  • Kept the existing GORM user_id IN (?) filter unchanged.
  • Removed unused encoding/base64 and encoding/json imports from the timeline handler.
  • Removed the timeline handler's local Redis client variable after its last direct Redis read was deleted.

Affected Files

  • src/Utils/Redis/Redis.go
  • src/Action/V1/Posts/TimeLinePostJustForYou.go

Resulting Data Flow

  1. The caller constructs the existing _list_followings_ Redis key.
  2. GetEncodedStringList reads the value through the shared Redis client.
  3. Missing values and Redis errors return an empty []string.
  4. Valid values are base64-decoded and unmarshalled into []string.
  5. Decode or unmarshal failures return an empty []string.
  6. The resulting slice is used by the existing PostgreSQL exclusion or GORM IN filter.

No database fallback, Redis write, retry, logging, or new abstraction was added.

Type Compatibility

The _list_followings_ payload represents user UUIDs as JSON strings. Redis.SuggestionUser already declared the decoded data as []string and passed it through pq.Array. Posts.TimeLinePostJustForYou only uses the decoded values as the arguments for user_id IN (?); GORM expands []string as query parameters in the same role previously served by []interface{}.

The change does not alter serialized API output because the followings slice is not returned to clients.

Scope Audit

The final repository scan reported:

  • 2 non-slim _list_followings_ readers using GetEncodedStringList.
  • 0 manual followings decoders in non-slim code.
  • 0 changed *Slim.go files.
  • Remaining manual followings readers exist only in excluded Slim handlers.

Verification

go vet ./...
git diff --check

Results:

  • The complete Go test suite passes with no failing package.
  • go vet ./... succeeds.
  • git diff --check succeeds.
  • Both changed Go files are formatted.

Problem

Two non-slim code paths manually read _list_followings_ Redis values using the same Redis GET, base64 decode, and JSON unmarshal sequence. The values use the same base64-encoded JSON string-array format already supported by Redis.GetEncodedStringList(ctx, key).

Keeping separate decoders duplicates error handling and allows the expected value type to drift between callers.

Scope

  • Replace the manual _list_followings_ decoder in Redis.SuggestionUser.
  • Replace the manual _list_followings_ decoder in Posts.TimeLinePostJustForYou.
  • Standardize the decoded value as []string.
  • Remove imports and local Redis client variables made unused by the refactor.
  • Preserve Redis keys, query filters, response shapes, ordering, pagination, and authorization behavior.
  • Keep every *Slim.go file unchanged.

Behavior Boundary

Redis.GetEncodedStringList returns an empty []string when Redis returns an error, the key is missing, the value is empty, base64 decoding fails, or JSON unmarshalling fails. The previous call sites ignored these errors and retained an empty slice, so failure behavior remains unchanged.

Posts.TimeLinePostJustForYou previously decoded the JSON array into []interface{}. The same Redis key was already decoded into []string by Redis.SuggestionUser, establishing that the stored values are strings. The timeline only passes the slice to GORM's IN filter, which accepts []string directly.

Out of Scope

  • Migrating Slim handlers.
  • Changing _list_followings_ writers or key names.
  • Adding Redis fallback, refresh, retry, or logging behavior.
  • Refactoring non-string Redis payloads.
  • Adding a specialized followings helper.

Acceptance Criteria

  • Both non-slim _list_followings_ readers use GetEncodedStringList.
  • No manual followings Redis/base64/JSON decoder remains in non-slim code.

Summary

Added the reusable Functions.Pagination utility and routed all 49 identical pagination flows through it. The implementation changes 44 handlers, the shared Functions file, and its test file. It removes 505 lines and adds 87 lines without adding dependencies or changing pagination behavior.

Changes

  • Replaced each exact manual block with one utility call.
  • Used _ for page in handlers that only consume limit and offset.
  • Kept page in 11 flows that expose it later in their response.
  • Added TestPagination for explicit query values and the default path.

  2. The utility reads the page and limit query values.
  3. Page zero becomes 1.
  4. Limit zero becomes the caller's supplied default.

Implementation: Batch Followed User Lookup

Summary

Added one shared followed-user batch lookup and applied it to five related user-list flows. Each flow now collects the current page's user IDs, performs at most one followers query, then reads followed values from a map while building the unchanged response.

Changes

  • Added UserFunctions.GetFollowedUserIDs in UsersFunctions.go.
  • Added the internal followedUserIDSet map builder.
  • Updated SearchUser.go.
  • Updated ProfileFollower.go.
  • Updated ProfileFollowing.go.
  • Updated SearchProfileFollower.go.
  • Updated SearchProfileFollowing.go.
  • Added UsersFunctions_test.go.
  • Added a comment in every caller explaining why IDs are collected before response construction.

The helper performs the equivalent of:

SELECT user_id
FROM followers
WHERE follower_id = :current_user_id
  AND user_id IN (:candidate_user_ids);

Returned IDs become a lookup map:

followedUserIDs[userID]

Go map lookup returns false when the user ID is absent, matching the previous default value.

Why Two Loops

The first in-memory loop extracts candidate IDs from the page result. The batch query must run after those IDs are known. The second loop builds or enriches the response using the completed lookup map.

The two O(N) memory loops replace N database round trips. Default page sizes are small, while avoiding repeated database queries removes the expensive part of the old flow.

  • The batch query uses the same relationship direction as the old checks: follower_id is the current user and user_id is the candidate user.

  • User ordering, pagination, filtering, hide, encryption, and response fields are unchanged.

Implementation: Centralize Previous Comment Request Setup

Summary

Added preparePreviousCommentRequest as a package-local helper and replaced the duplicated setup in the two previous-comment endpoints. Authentication state, pagination, blocked-post validation state, and excluded-user data now come from one implementation without changing either API response.

Changes

  • Added PreviousCommentRequest.go containing:
    • previousCommentRequest
    • preparePreviousCommentRequest
  • Updated ListPreviousComment.go to use the prepared request.
  • Updated ListPreviousReplyComment.go to use the prepared request.
  • Replaced duplicated manual pagination with the existing Functions.Pagination(c, 20) utility.
  • Removed unused context, Redis, and user-function imports from both callers.

Each caller now starts its shared setup with:

request := preparePreviousCommentRequest(c)
if request.unauthorized {
	return Functions.ErrorResponse(c, 401, fiber.ErrUnauthorized.Message, "Unauthorized")
}
if request.blockedPost {
	return Functions.ErrorResponse(c, 403, fiber.ErrForbidden.Message, "You blocked this post", "blocked")
}

The callers still own the exact HTTP responses. The helper only reports the existing authentication and blocked-post states, avoiding hidden response writes inside request preparation.

Shared Flow

preparePreviousCommentRequest now performs the matching flow once:

  1. Read the current user's encryption identifier.
  2. Retrieve user data and report invalid authentication state.
  3. Read last_login, sid, and commentSid.
  4. Calculate pagination with default limit 20.
  5. Load blocked posts and stop preparation when the target post is blocked.
  6. Load blocked and deactivated users.
  7. Combine those users into notInEncrypt.

Behavior Compatibility

  • Invalid user data still produces the same HTTP 401 response from each caller.
  • A blocked target post still produces the same HTTP 403 response with input blocked.
  • The helper stops before loading user exclusion lists when authentication fails or the post is blocked, matching the previous execution order.
  • Functions.Pagination(c, 20) has the same page, limit, and offset calculation previously duplicated in both files.
  • The previous-comment and previous-reply SQL queries remain in their original endpoints.

Implementation: Batch Search User Posts

Summary

Replaced the per-user post query in SearchUser with one package-local batch query. The query uses a PostgreSQL window function to preserve the old maximum of four newest posts for each user. Results are grouped by user ID and assigned to the unchanged response model.

Changes

  • Added SearchUserPosts.go containing:
    • searchUserPostRow
    • getSearchUserPosts
    • searchUserPostsQuery
    • groupSearchUserPosts
  • Updated SearchUser.go to collect user IDs once.
  • Reused the same user-ID slice for followed-status and post batch lookups.
  • Removed the post query from the response loop.
  • Added SearchUserPosts_test.go.
  • Kept a code comment explaining why ID collection occurs before response construction.

Batch Query

The new query performs the equivalent of:

SELECT user_id, slug, thumbnail
FROM (
    SELECT user_id, slug, thumbnail,
        ROW_NUMBER() OVER (
            PARTITION BY user_id
            ORDER BY created_at DESC
        ) AS post_rank
    FROM posts
    WHERE user_id IN (:user_ids)
      AND visibility = 'public'
      AND post_type != 'video360'
      AND is_publish = true
) AS ranked_posts
WHERE post_rank <= 4
ORDER BY user_id, post_rank;

post_rank is an internal query value. It replaces the old LIMIT 4 executed separately for each user and is not selected by the outer query or returned by the API.

Why Per-User Ranking Is Required

A single global LIMIT 4 would return only four posts across all searched users. ROW_NUMBER() restarts numbering for each user_id because of PARTITION BY user_id:

user A: 1, 2, 3, 4, 5
user B: 1, 2, 3, 4, 5

Filtering with post_rank <= 4 therefore preserves the previous maximum of four posts for user A and four posts for user B.

Response Compatibility

  • The outer query returns only user_id, slug, and thumbnail; post_rank never reaches the model response.
  • Rows are ordered by user ID and rank before grouping, preserving newest-first order within each user's slice.
  • groupSearchUserPosts initializes every requested user ID with []Models.SearchUserPost{}.
  • Missing posts therefore remain posts: [], not null.
  • The same visibility, post type, publication status, and creation-time ordering are applied.
  • Batch query errors remain non-fatal, matching the previous ignored post-query error behavior.
  • The main search result and followed-status response remain unchanged.

After:

Summary

Replaced per-user CheckFollowed calls in ListLikePost and ListLikeComment with the existing global GetFollowedUserIDs batch utility. Each like-list page now needs at most one follower query.

Changes

ListLikePost.go

  • Collects IDs from []Models.LikedUser before response shaping.
  • Calls UserFunctions.GetFollowedUserIDs once for authenticated users.
  • Reads each user's followed state from map[string]bool.

Before, per endpoint:

1 like-list query + N followed-state queries

1 like-list query + at most 1 followed-state query

SELECT user_id
FROM followers
WHERE follower_id = :authenticated_user_id
  AND user_id IN (:listed_user_ids);

The first loop only collects user IDs required by the batch query. The second loop shapes the existing API response after the followed-state map is available. This prevents a database query inside the response loop while preserving the returned order.

Implementation: Batch Elasticsearch Post Counts

Summary

Added ElasticSearch.RetrieveElasticBatch and replaced per-post Elasticsearch GET requests in five post-list flows with one _mget request per page. The utility preserves raw _source JSON and omits missing documents so each caller can retain its original fallback format.

Affected APIs

  • Timeline Recent.
  • Timeline JustForYou.
  • Most Popular Post.
  • Nearest Post.
  • Collection Post Detail.

The first three APIs share enrichTimelinePosts, so their batching is owned by one implementation point in PostResponse.go.

Utility

src/Utils/ElasticSearch/ElasticSearch.go now provides:

func RetrieveElasticBatch(index string, documentIDs []string) (map[string]json.RawMessage, error)

The utility:

  • Returns an empty map immediately for an empty ID slice.
  • Encodes all document IDs into one _mget request body.
  • Reuses the existing Elasticsearch client configuration.
  • Closes the response body after decoding.
  • Maps every found _source to its _id.
  • Omits missing documents instead of returning an error.

The request is equivalent to:

POST /post_<prefix>/_mget
Content-Type: application/json

{"ids":["post_<slug-1>","post_<slug-2>"]}

Timeline Enrichment

PostResponse.go now:

  1. Builds document IDs in the same order as the post slice.
  2. Retrieves all counter sources once.
  3. Looks up each source by its document ID.
  4. Decodes found sources into the existing map[string]interface{} representation.
  5. Passes the unchanged value to applyTimelinePostData.

The obsolete Fiber context parameter was removed from enrichTimelinePosts because Elasticsearch response writing is no longer performed inside that helper. Recent, JustForYou, MostPopular, and the existing empty-list test were updated for the smaller signature.

Nearest and Collection Enrichment

NearestPost and CollectionPostDetail collect document IDs before their response loops. Found sources are wrapped directly in postgres.Jsonb, preserving the previous raw JSON representation.

When a source is missing:

  • NearestPost retains {"counter_view":0,"counter_like":0,"counter_comment":0}.
  • CollectionPostDetail continues using the existing postCount fallback with the same JSON value.

Response Compatibility

  • Posts remain in the database query's original order because the response loops still iterate the original slices.
  • Counter documents are matched by ID, not by Elasticsearch response position.
  • JSON numbers are not converted for raw postgres.Jsonb responses.
  • Timeline sources are decoded into the same map type used by the previous single-document utility.
  • Empty _source objects still trigger the timeline's existing zero-counter default.
  • Missing documents still produce fallback counters instead of an API failure.
  • Description, bookmark, filtering, pagination, encryption, and response schemas remain unchanged.

Query Impact

Before, per affected page:

1 post-list database query + N Elasticsearch GET requests

After:

1 post-list database query + at most 1 Elasticsearch _mget request

Batch Thumbnail Query

The thumbnail query performs the equivalent of:

SELECT folder_id, thumbnail
FROM (
    SELECT
        folder_id,
        thumbnail,
        ROW_NUMBER() OVER (
            PARTITION BY folder_id
            ORDER BY created_at DESC
        ) AS thumbnail_rank
    FROM views_list_bookmarks
    WHERE folder_id IN (:folder_ids)
      AND user_id = :user_id
      AND post_type != 'video360'
      AND slug NOT IN (:blocked_posts)
      AND encrypt NOT IN (:excluded_users)
) AS ranked_bookmarks
WHERE thumbnail_rank <= 4
ORDER BY folder_id, thumbnail_rank;

The two NOT IN clauses are only added when their corresponding exclusion lists are non-empty, matching the previous queries.

PARTITION BY folder_id is required because a global LIMIT 4 would return only four thumbnails across the complete page. Ranking restarts for each folder and therefore preserves the previous per-folder limit.

POTD states use one query equivalent to:

SELECT DISTINCT folder_id
FROM broadcast
WHERE folder_id IN (:folder_ids);

Counter documents use one request equivalent to:

Implementation: Batch Search Hashtag Posts

Summary

Replaced the per-hashtag post-preview query in SearchHashtag with one package-local batch query. PostgreSQL ROW_NUMBER() partitions rows by tag so each hashtag still receives at most four posts. Results are grouped by tag and assigned to the unchanged response model.

Changes

  • Added SearchHashtagPosts.go containing:
    • searchHashtagPostRow
    • getSearchHashtagPosts

Batch Query

The new query performs the equivalent of:

SELECT tag, slug, thumbnail
FROM (
    SELECT tag, slug, thumbnail,
        ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY tag) AS post_rank
    FROM views_hashtag
    WHERE tag IN (:tags)
) AS ranked_posts
WHERE post_rank <= 4
ORDER BY tag, post_rank;

post_rank is internal. It replaces the separate LIMIT 4 calls and is not returned by the API.

A global LIMIT 4 would return four posts across all hashtags. PARTITION BY tag restarts ROW_NUMBER() for every tag, so post_rank <= 4 keeps up to four posts for each hashtag.

No ordering expression was added inside ROW_NUMBER(). The previous query had no ORDER BY, so adding one would introduce new response behavior.
